currentState.summary: The browser window computes canvas backing dimensions from CSS content bounds multiplied by window.devicePixelRatio, configures the WGPU surface to that physical size, stores DPR as the GPUI scale factor, and Swash rasterizes glyphs at font_size multiplied by that scale. Despite that scale path, WebWindow::is_subpixel_rendering_supported returns false unconditionally. Window::paint_glyph therefore creates MonochromeSprite glyphs for every WASM text frame, while WgpuRenderer's existing dual-source SubpixelSprite pipeline remains unreachable. The prior regression intentionally made this choice to eliminate RGB fringes and asserted zero glyph channel spread, but its crop metric did not compare spatial edge sharpness with a matched browser-native reference. The current Test Suite text-quality page has light/dark RayX specimens and aggregate edge energy only; it lacks fractional DPR, scale-tuple assertions, crop-local typography matching, dynamic scale transitions, and a quality threshold that rejects visibly soft glyphs.

decisions.title: Replace subjective and whole-page quality checks with a matched physical-pixel authority
decisions.decision: Create a focused Test Suite vertical slice with visible RayX WebGPU and browser-native DOM specimens using the same bundled font bytes and authored typography. Capture explicit crop rectangles and compute luminance edge-transition width, acutance, stem contrast, chromatic-fringe energy outside the matched reference edge band, glyph bounds, and advances per DPR/theme/font cell. Record renderer/scale metadata with every crop and run the complete matrix serially three times for final proof.
decisions.rationale: The user-visible defect is spatial softness. The existing aggregate edge-energy/channel-count test can pass soft grayscale glyphs and cannot distinguish text from colored UI. A matched browser-native crop on the same compositor provides an attributable reference without inventing a second renderer.

decisions.title: Treat browser scale as one atomic logical/physical generation
decisions.decision: Keep window.devicePixelRatio authoritative and preserve native-DPR canvas allocation. Commit CSS logical size, rounded backing size, WGPU surface size, GPUI scene scale, and scale-dependent glyph cache identity as one observable generation. Coalesce ResizeObserver/media-query signals, force a fresh draw for a changed generation, and prove live transitions through Chromium device-metrics emulation. Change production calculus only where the new tuple assertions demonstrate an actual mismatch.
decisions.rationale: The source path appears mathematically consistent but the real monitor report requires runtime proof at fractional scale and live transitions. Treating the tuple atomically prevents a new surface from presenting stale scene/glyph pixels and avoids masking a calculus bug with text antialiasing changes.

decisions.title: Select the smallest browser glyph strategy through a frozen candidate ladder
decisions.decision: After Sprint 1 freezes the matched baseline and Sprint 2 proves scale truth, execute one checkpointed AgentX improvement loop with atomic commit-or-revert candidates in this order: (1) correct any proven glyph sampling-phase, atlas-coordinate, or gamma/contrast defect in the existing grayscale path; (2) correct existing Swash hinting/raster parameters without changing geometry; (3) add glyph-local higher-resolution coverage plus an explicit quality downsample only if native grayscale cannot meet the gate; (4) permit the existing dual-source LCD path only for an opaque, axis-aligned, exact-device-mapping browser state when it independently passes the chromatic-fringe gate. Stop at the first smallest candidate that satisfies every quality, compatibility, and resource contract; retain grayscale fallback for every unsafe/unsupported state. If no candidate passes, leave the epic blocked and reconcile the design instead of shipping a partial improvement.
decisions.rationale: Current evidence identifies grayscale-only policy but does not prove whether softness comes from scale, sampling, gamma/hinting, or insufficient physical coverage. A fixed causal ladder prevents a costly supersampling or fragile LCD solution from being accepted before simpler correctness repairs are exhausted, while still giving implementation a deterministic end state and stop condition.

decisions.title: Make every pixel-changing glyph parameter part of cache identity
decisions.decision: Reuse RenderGlyphParams and GlyphCacheKey as the single glyph identity boundary. Include the accepted coverage mode, actual scene scale, subpixel phase, and any distinct glyph-local raster/downsample scale that changes atlas pixels. Reuse unchanged entries, avoid global cache flushes for idempotent observations, and ensure a live scale/mode transition cannot draw a stale entry.
decisions.rationale: Improved pixels are incorrect if an old grayscale/scale entry is reused after DPR or policy changes. Extending the existing cache key is simpler and safer than adding a second atlas/cache or clearing the complete atlas on every viewport signal.
